suggestions: Log the time each value describes, not the end of its window

Your values describe audio about 30 ms before the logged timestamp. Comparing logs to a dataset at face value gives 48.5% pitch accuracy instead of 85.0%. Formants within 10% drop from 94.2% to 62.8% (F1).

Each feature uses a different amount of recent audio: pitch the last 50 ms, formants the last 100 ms (read at the middle, so 50 ms back), vocal weight the last 256 samples. In main11's logger, store the window centre per feature (for example pitch_time = t - 0.025, formant_time = t - 0.05), or shift audio_timestamp back by a single agreed amount. Any dataset comparison should use these times.
Add a real voicing check instead of loudness + zero-crossing gates

18.6% of frames with no voice still get a pitch (Praat 3.4%). Your get_pitch only checks loudness (RMS > 0.001) and zero-crossing rate, and librosa.yin always returns some pitch, so any quiet hum or breath that passes both gates gets a pitch. 57% of these frames are within 50 ms of real voicing, where the analysis window still holds the start or end of a voiced sound. The typical one is only 20 dB below the loudest frame, so it is not quiet noise. A loudness gate tied to each recording's noise floor barely helps (voicing error 14.8% at best becomes 14.1%), so the fix has to look at periodicity.

Add a periodicity test: librosa.pyin's voiced probability, Praat's voicing threshold, or YIN's own aperiodicity value (reject frames above about 0.2-0.3). Judge voicing on the newest 20-30 ms rather than the whole 50 ms window so it switches off sooner after a vowel ends, and require 2-3 voiced frames in a row before reporting a pitch to remove one-frame blips.
Stop using zero-crossing rate to reject noisy frames

Pitch accuracy falls to 63.0% at 10 dB and 35.5% at 5 dB SNR. At 10 dB, 100% of the voiced frames you miss were thrown out by the zero-crossing gate, because noise adds zero crossings even when a voice is clearly there. The candidate fix (Praat on the same 100 ms window) keeps 78.5% at 10 dB.
Replace the ZCR > 0.15 rule with a periodicity measure (see the voicing suggestion). For live use, a microphone with noise suppression off plus a periodicity-based gate is more reliable than ZCR.
Widen the pitch search range

In the PTDB recordings, 482 voiced frames are below 75 Hz (deep or creaky male voices), and only 9.1% of them get a correct pitch. Synthetic voices at 700, 900, 1200 Hz come out an octave low (half the true pitch). get_pitch searches 75.0-600.0 Hz.

Use fmin around 55-60 Hz and fmax around 1000-1100 Hz (your notes mention singing up to 1000-2000 Hz). YIN needs at least two periods of the lowest pitch in its frame, so pass frame_length explicitly (about 2.5/fmin seconds of samples) instead of librosa's default of 2048 samples, which is a different duration at every sample rate.
Smooth out octave jumps over time
4.7% of your voiced frames are more than 20% off (Praat 2.1%), 1.7% are octave jumps. Each frame is estimated on its own, so nothing stops a single frame from jumping an octave.

Keep the last few pitch values and reject a new value that jumps by about an octave unless the jump persists for 2-3 frames (or run a median filter over the last 3-5 frames). pYIN and Praat do this with a Viterbi path. This per-frame error data is also exactly what the correction network idea (learning true values from recent frames) would train on.
Rebuild the base spectral slope

It barely reacts to voice brightness (rank correlation +0.10, total change 0.9 across a 12 dB/octave range), while the derived slope tracks it perfectly (+1.00). The fit runs over every FFT bin up to 4500 Hz with a -60 dB floor, so the many high, quiet bins and the floor dominate the line.

Fit dB against log-frequency on band energies (for example octave bands from 100 to 4000 Hz) or use a standard measure such as the alpha ratio (energy 50-1000 Hz vs 1-5 kHz) or the Hammarberg index. Or drop it and keep the derived slope.
Make vocal weight independent of pitch, loudness and sample rate

Changing pitch moves vocal weight 1.1x as much as the full brightness range (loudness 0.43x, sample rate 0.29x). It also jumps 29% of its useful range from one frame to the next on a perfectly steady vowel. It analyses only 256 samples (5.3 ms at 48 kHz, 16 ms at 16 kHz), which is less than one pitch period for most voices, and log(energy + 1) depends on the input level.

Use a fixed duration (25-40 ms) instead of a fixed sample count, resample to one rate first, normalise the frame's level before taking logs, and average over a few frames. Then re-run this benchmark: the pitch and loudness ratios should fall well below 0.5.
Choose the formant ceiling from the voice instead of always 5500 Hz

The Praat ceiling sweep picks men 5000 Hz, women 5500 Hz, boys 5500 Hz, girls 5500 Hz. A ceiling chosen from the detected pitch (the candidate fix) raises F3 within-10% for girls by 4.5 points, but lowers F3 for boys by 1.6. Averaged over F1-F3 for everyone the change is +0.8 points. Pitch alone is a rough guide to vocal tract length, which is what the ceiling should follow.

Rather than a fixed pitch rule, try 2-3 ceilings in get_formants_praat and keep the one whose formant tracks are smoothest over the last few frames (the Escudero et al. 2009 method). Let a user setting override it, since a trained voice can have a high pitch with a long vocal tract.
Fix the spectral slope unit on the dashboard
The slope is fitted against log10(frequency), so it is in dB per decade (per 10x in frequency). The dashboard readout says dB/kHz.
Change the label to dB/decade, or divide by 3.32 and call it dB/octave, the unit most voice research uses.
Check the breath (noise) rolloff
Adding breath noise barely changes it (rank correlation +0.20), so it does not measure breathiness yet. The helper named for an 85% rolloff actually uses 98%.
Use harmonics-to-noise ratio (Praat's to_harmonicity, or the cepstral peak prominence CPP) as the breathiness measure. Both are standard and have published norms.
The 2-second noise calibration currently has no effect
get_audio_data receives noise_power_profile but never uses it (the denoised harmonic function is commented out). The live mode waits 2 s at startup for nothing.
Either use it, for example to set the voicing loudness gate from the room's noise level (see above), or skip the recording.
